newsitem.title: USA: Sara Lee sees low double-digit EPS gains in '97.
newsitem.headline: Sara Lee sees low double-digit EPS gains in '97.

text.p: Sara Lee Corp Chairman John Bryan said Thursday the company expects to increase earnings per share for fiscal 1997 by a low double-digit growth rate.
In fiscal 1996, Sara Lee, a food and consumer products company, earned $1.83 a share.

Bryan told reporters after the company's annual shareholders meeting here, that fiscal 1997 earnings would have to be in a range of $2.00 a share to $2.10 in order to meet the low double-digit growth rate.
Bryan said Sara Lee also has set a goal of achieving return on invested capital (ROIC) of 40 percent in the near future. In fiscal 1996, ROIC was 38 percent, a record level for the company.
"Our major strategy is to go to the mid-40s" percent ROIC, Bryan said.

To do that, Sara Lee will take a hard look at some of its lesser-performing businesses, many of which are in the company's personal products division, Bryan said. "Some of them we will actually fix, some we will close and some we will sell," he added. "Those are words that are carefully chosen."
He declined to specify businesses, but said that most of them are in Europe with "a couple" in the United States.
Sara Lee's personal products include hosiery, knit wear and intimate apparel.
Bryan, who recently turned 60, said his top priority is helping to find a successor when he retires in about five years.
Bryan became president of the company in 1974 and was named chief executive officer in 1975. He was elected chairman of the board in 1976.
He said he knew of a "half a dozen names" of potential internal candidates for the top job, but gave no other specifics.
